findings.reason: moving the fix inside `write` (hand `snapshots`' paths plus the aggregate to `_commit_state_write`) closes five call sites with no signature change and no re-derived list, where s2's placement leaves the same silent-uncommitted-write defect in production on four paths it explicitly excludes.
findings.text: s2 adds a caller-supplied `changed_paths` out-parameter to `write` and has `record_hold_checks` pass it, but `write` already computes exactly those paths as `snapshots` from `_keep_run_files_identical` (`reckon/ledger.py:1899`, called at `2174`), and `write(commit=True)` passes only the aggregate `path` to `_commit_state_write` (`reckon/ledger.py:2192-2200`), so the identical defect is live on four further callers (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3561`, `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:1082`, `reckon/crew/routing.py:3003` and `:3130`) which s2 states are left untouched

findings.reason: a worker must either invent a reason channel through a two-caller boolean function or drop an assertion its gate names, so the node cannot reach one verdict as written.
findings.text: s3 says `_ask_session_host` "returns False with the same reason `_rearm_session_follower` (near line 785) gives today", but `_ask_session_host` returns `bool` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:746`) and carries no reason string, while the ownership reason exists only in `_rearm_session_follower`'s own pre-check; the s3 done-when then asserts an ask "returns False with the ownership reason", which a boolean cannot carry

findings.reason: the pointer lands inside the right function and nothing is deleted, so a worker reading the function finds the comment and corrects the right sentence.
findings.text: s2 says "The `record_hold_checks` docstring's claim that run rows stay byte-identical is corrected", but that claim is an inline comment inside the function body (`reckon/ledger.py`, the aggregate-load comment preceding the loop), not in the docstring, whose text says it "commits the aggregate it rewrote at once" and says nothing about run rows

findings.reason: `record_hold_checks` is the public function the done-when calls directly and its one live caller verifies the path runs, so naming it sharpens the evidence without altering the mechanism.
findings.text: s2 names `record_hold_checks` as the actor driving `write` but never names its caller, `reckon/budget.py:1911`, which is the single production entry point through which a hold transition reaches the rewritten run record

response_events.note: §2 now moves the fix inside write: write's commit=True branch stages the run files in its snapshots (from _keep_run_files_identical, ledger.py near line 1899) with the aggregate, closing its four other callers too, and the changed_paths list record_hold_checks reads is filled from those same snapshots, not re-derived.

§3's ownership check now lives in _ask_session_host_for_follower, which returns False and writes no request; the case asserts exactly that, and the reason string stays where it is, in _rearm_session_follower.
